newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil castor seed crop to reach five-year high.
newsitem.headline: Brazil castor seed crop to reach five-year high.

text.p: Brazil's castor seed production is expected to recover to its highest level in five years in 1996/97 but it will remain a net importer of the oilseed, the Ministry of Agriculture's National Supply Company (Conab) said.
Brazil is forecast to produce 110,400 tonnes of castor seed in 1996/97, up from 47,600 in 1995/96, Conab said in its latest grain crop forecast.
"The last harvest of a comparable size was in 1991/92, when Brazil produced 116,000 tonnes," said an economist at the agency. "But there is no indication that Brazil will start exporting."
The rise was due mainly to a productivity improvement in the Barreiras region of Bahia following important investments in technology, the economist said.
Brazil currently imports castor seeds and exports hydrogenated and dehydrated castor oil, as well as refined castor oil to a lesser extent.
Exports of hydrogenated and dehydrated castor oil totaled 18,874 tonnes in 1996, down from 25,355 tonnes in 1995. Refined oil exports fell to 1,018 tonnes in 1996 from 4,317 tonnes the previous year.
The Finance Ministry said it was currently unable to provide detailed import data.
